sections.heading: How do muscles work?
sections.text: Muscles are made up of thousands of small elastic fibers, similar to rubber bands, that contract and relax to cause movement. When the fibers contract, they get shorter, which pulls the bones they’re connected to closer together.

sections.heading: Skeletal muscles
sections.text: Skeletal (SKEH-luh-tuhl) muscles help you move, sit up straight, and keep your balance. Skeletal muscles are sometimes called voluntary muscles because you can control them.

sections.heading: Cardiac muscles
sections.text: Cardiac (KAAR-dee-ak) muscles make up the heart. Like smooth muscles, cardiac muscles are involuntary. They contract and relax automatically to pump blood through your body.
